# tld.h

Single-header C toolbox: allocation and error macros, terminal messages, strings, a hash map, JSON, random numbers, statistics, sorting, a k-d tree, a thread pool, text templates and file helpers.

tld.h is GENERATED by tools/amalgamate.py from src/: do not edit it; change src/ and
regenerate. Manual: docs/tld.md, generated from tld.h by tools/tlddoc.c.

Every public symbol of tld.h is documented below, module by module, with its declaration; the [index](#index) at the end lists them alphabetically. Implementation: define TLD_IMPLEMENTATION in one .c file (see Usage).

<a id="sec-usage"></a>

## Usage

In exactly one .c file of your program, before any other #include:

```c
#define TLD_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "tld.h"
```

and plain #include "tld.h" everywhere else. C11 plus POSIX (pthreads, stat,
realpath); macOS and Linux. Build: cc -std=c11 prog.c -lm -lpthread.

<a id="sec-errors"></a>

## Errors

A function that can fail returns int: OK (0) on success, FAIL (1) on failure, with
its results in pointer arguments; one that returns a pointer returns NULL on
failure. Failures print an ERROR line (time, message, file and line) to stderr;
lookups that just find nothing (tld_hash_get, tld_path_exists, tld_json_get_*, ...)
return FAIL silently. A few functions return a plain value or a 1/0 truth value
instead; each one says so. Nothing exits or aborts.

RUN(call), ASSERT(test, fmt, ...), ERROR_MSG(fmt, ...) and the allocation macros
MMALLOC, MREALLOC, MMALLOC_ALIGNED and galloc jump to a label named ERROR in the
calling function on failure. The usual shape of a function:

```c
int load(const char *path, tld_strbuf **out)
{
        tld_strbuf *b = NULL;
        ASSERT(path != NULL, "No path");
        RUN(tld_strbuf_alloc(&b, 256));
        RUN(tld_strbuf_append(b, path));
        *out = b;
        return OK;
ERROR:
        tld_strbuf_free(b);
        return FAIL;
}
```

Initialise every pointer to NULL: MMALLOC refuses a non-NULL pointer, and the
cleanup after ERROR: may run before an allocation happened.

LOG_MSG, WARNING_MSG, ERROR_MSG, ASSERT and the rich-output calls take a printf
format, checked by the compiler. Print text from users or files with "%s", never as
the format itself: LOG_MSG("%s", line), not LOG_MSG(line).

<a id="sec-memory"></a>

## Memory

Objects come from an allocator (tld_strbuf_alloc(&b, ...), tld_hash_alloc,
tld_tld_kdtree_alloc, tld_rng_alloc, tld_json_parse, TLD_JSON_OBJECT, ...) and belong to the caller,
who frees them with the matching free function (tld_strbuf_free, tld_hash_free,
tld_tld_kdtree_free, tld_rng_free, tld_json_obj_free, ...); every free function accepts NULL.
galloc memory is freed with gfree, MMALLOC memory with MFREE, never with free();
both set the pointer to NULL, so freeing again on an error path is harmless.
Pointers handed out by an object (tld_hash_get, tld_json_get_str, ...) are borrowed
and const: valid until that object changes or is freed; never write through them
or free them. Sizes are int-based: a string buffer holds at most INT32_MAX - 1 bytes
and refuses to grow past that.

<a id="sec-threads"></a>

## Threads

Objects have no locks: use each one from one thread at a time. The tld_thread_pool_*
calls and tld_logsum_init are thread-safe; tld_progress and the TLD_START_TIMER timer keep
global state.

<a id="sec-environment"></a>

## Environment

```text
TLD_VERBOSE  0 errors only, 1 normal (default), 2 also DEBUG_MSG lines
NO_COLOR     set and non-empty: no colour on stderr (likewise TERM=dumb)
```

<a id="sec-limitations"></a>

## Limitations

JSON integers that fit in 32 bits are stored exactly; larger ones are stored as
double, exact only up to 2^53 (9007199254740992), so bigger values lose precision.
JSON parsing is strict (RFC 8259): True, NaN, leading zeros and trailing commas are
rejected. JSON keys containing '.' or '[' cannot be addressed by path.
tld_progress keeps one bar at a time and is not for concurrent use from threads.
POSIX only (macOS, Linux, other Unix); not Windows except through WSL.

<a id="mod-core"></a>

## core

`src/core/tld-core.h`: Return codes (OK/FAIL), the error-handling macros RUN, ASSERT and ERROR_MSG that jump to a local ERROR label, timestamped log messages and rich terminal output on stderr. No message changes errno, so code can log and then report it. Every other module builds on these.

<a id="TLD_API"></a>

### `TLD_API`

```c
#ifndef TLD_API
#ifdef __cplusplus
#define TLD_API extern "C"
#else
#define TLD_API extern
#endif
#endif
```

TLD_API: the linkage of every public tld function and variable, extern (extern "C" in
C++). Define it before including tld.h to add attributes (visibility, dllexport).

<a id="OK"></a><a id="FAIL"></a>

### `OK`, `FAIL`

```c
#define OK              0
#define FAIL            1
```

Return codes of every tld function that can fail: OK (0) on success, FAIL (1) on
failure. Compare with == OK; do not use the result as a boolean.

<a id="TLD_MIN"></a><a id="TLD_MAX"></a>

### `TLD_MIN`, `TLD_MAX`

```c
#define TLD_MIN(a,b)          TLD__MINMAX(<, a, b, __COUNTER__)
#define TLD_MAX(a,b)          TLD__MINMAX(>, a, b, __COUNTER__)
```

Smaller / larger of a and b, with the usual arithmetic conversions (int and double
give double). Each argument is evaluated exactly once, so TLD_MAX(i++, n) is safe.
A GNU statement expression (gcc, clang): not for constant expressions such as a
file-scope array size.

<a id="LOG_MSG"></a><a id="WARNING_MSG"></a>

### `LOG_MSG`, `WARNING_MSG`

```c
#define LOG_MSG(...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__message(TLD__MSG_LOG, __VA_ARGS__))
#define WARNING_MSG(...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__message(TLD__MSG_WARNING, __VA_ARGS__))
```

LOG_MSG(fmt, ...) / WARNING_MSG(fmt, ...): print a timestamped LOG or WARNING line
(printf-style, newline added) to stderr and continue. Silent when TLD_VERBOSE=0.

<a id="ERROR_MSG"></a>

### `ERROR_MSG`

```c
#define ERROR_MSG(...) do {                                     \
                TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__);                      \
                tld__message_at(TLD__MSG_ERROR, __FILE__, __LINE__, __VA_ARGS__); \
                goto ERROR;                                     \
        }while (0)
```

ERROR_MSG(fmt, ...): print a timestamped ERROR line with file and line to stderr
(always, whatever TLD_VERBOSE says) and goto ERROR.

<a id="RUN"></a>

### `RUN`

```c
#define RUN(EXP) do {                                           \
                if((EXP) != OK){                                \
                        tld__message_at(TLD__MSG_ERROR, __FILE__, __LINE__, "%s", TLD__FAILED(EXP)); \
                        goto ERROR;                             \
                }                                               \
        } while (0)
```

RUN(EXP): evaluate EXP (a call returning OK/FAIL); if it is not OK, print
Function "EXP" failed. as an ERROR line with file and line and goto ERROR.

<a id="ASSERT"></a>

### `ASSERT`

```c
#define ASSERT(TEST,...) ...
```

ASSERT(TEST, fmt, ...): if TEST is false, print "Assertion failed: TEST" and the
printf-style message as ERROR lines (with file and line) and goto ERROR. The message
is required. Active in all builds; the enclosing function needs an ERROR: label.

<a id="tld_verbosity"></a>

### `tld_verbosity`

```c
TLD_API int tld_verbosity(void);
```

The TLD_VERBOSE level: 0, 1 (the default, also for unset or unparsable values) or 2.
A single digit is accepted; the variable is read on every call.

<a id="tld_term_has_color"></a>

### `tld_term_has_color`

```c
TLD_API int tld_term_has_color(void);
```

1 if stderr gets colour: it is a terminal, NO_COLOR is unset or empty and TERM is
not "dumb"; 0 otherwise.

<a id="SECTION_MSG"></a><a id="KV_MSG"></a><a id="OK_MSG"></a><a id="DEBUG_MSG"></a>

### `SECTION_MSG`, `KV_MSG`, `OK_MSG`, `DEBUG_MSG`

```c
#define SECTION_MSG(...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__section(__VA_ARGS__))
#define KV_MSG(KEY, ...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__kv(KEY, __VA_ARGS__))
#define OK_MSG(...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__ok(__VA_ARGS__))
#define DEBUG_MSG(...) (TLD__LITERAL(__VA_ARGS__), tld__debug(__VA_ARGS__))
```

Rich terminal output. Everything goes to stderr, so stdout keeps only a program's
results. Colour and symbols are used only when stderr is a terminal and NO_COLOR is
not set. TLD_VERBOSE sets how much is shown: 0 errors only, 1 normal (default),
2 also DEBUG_MSG lines.

```text
SECTION_MSG("Aligning %d sequences", n);   ── Aligning 40 sequences ──────────
KV_MSG("model", "%s", name);                  model     inkling-2-mini:latest
OK_MSG("done in %.1f s", t);                ✓ done in 1.9 s
DEBUG_MSG("seed %u", seed);                 · seed 42          (TLD_VERBOSE=2)
tld_progress(i + 1, n, "aligning");        aligning [#######.....]  58% 23/40
```

<a id="tld_progress"></a>

### `tld_progress`

```c
TLD_API void tld_progress(long done, long total, const char *label);
```

Progress of a loop: call with done = 1..total. On a terminal one line is redrawn
(only when the percentage changes); otherwise only the final line is printed. Not
meant to be called from several threads at once.

<a id="mod-alloc"></a>

## alloc

`src/alloc/tld-alloc.h`: Checked allocation macros (MMALLOC, MREALLOC, MFREE) and galloc/gfree, which allocate zeroed, typed 1D arrays and 2D matrices that remember their dimensions. All allocation macros goto ERROR on failure.

<a id="MMALLOC"></a>

### `MMALLOC`

```c
#define MMALLOC(p, size) ...
```

MMALLOC(p, size): p = malloc(size), zero-filled. p must be NULL beforehand and size
non-zero; either mistake, or running out of memory, prints an error and does goto
ERROR. Free with MFREE.

<a id="MMALLOC_ALIGNED"></a>

### `MMALLOC_ALIGNED`

```c
#define MMALLOC_ALIGNED(p, size, align) ...
```

MMALLOC_ALIGNED: like MMALLOC, for a struct whose declaration asks for more alignment
than malloc guarantees (16 bytes on 64-bit), e.g. __attribute__((aligned(64))). Using
plain malloc for such a struct breaks the promise the declaration makes to the compiler
(undefined behaviour; UBSan reports "misaligned address ... requires 64 byte alignment").
Pass the struct's own alignment: MMALLOC_ALIGNED(p, sizeof(struct s), _Alignof(struct s)).
C11 aligned_alloc requires the size to be a multiple of the alignment, so the size is
rounded up. The block is freed with plain free(), so MFREE works unchanged.

<a id="MREALLOC"></a>

### `MREALLOC`

```c
#define MREALLOC(p, size) ...
```

MREALLOC(p, size): resize p to size bytes (malloc when p is NULL). Bytes beyond the old
size are not zeroed. On failure p is unchanged, an error is printed and goto ERROR;
size 0 is an error.

<a id="MFREE"></a>

### `MFREE`

```c
#define MFREE(p)                                                        \
        do {                                                            \
                free(p);                                                \
                (p) = NULL;                                             \
        } while (0)
```

MFREE(p): free(p) and set p to NULL. For memory from MMALLOC, MREALLOC or malloc (use
gfree for galloc memory). p must be an lvalue; a NULL p is fine.

<a id="galloc"></a>

### `galloc`

```c
#define galloc(...) TLD__GALLOC_ARGS(__VA_ARGS__)
```

galloc(&a, n): a = zeroed array of n elements of a's element type.
galloc(&m, n, k): m = zeroed n x k matrix, used as m[i][j]; the rows share one
contiguous block. Any element type (numbers, pointers, structs) whose alignment malloc
provides; a more strictly aligned type is a compile error. The pointer should be NULL (an existing block is not freed or resized). On
failure an error is printed and goto ERROR. Free with gfree; tld_galloc_dim1/tld_galloc_dim2 give
the dimensions back.

<a id="gfree"></a>

### `gfree`

```c
#define gfree(a)                                                        \
        do {                                                            \
                tld__gfree(a);                                            \
                (a) = NULL;                                             \
        } while (0)
```

gfree(p): free memory from galloc (1D or 2D) and set p to NULL, like MFREE, so a
second gfree(p) on an error path is harmless. p must be an lvalue (a variable, field
or element); a NULL p is fine. Never pass galloc memory to free() or MFREE.

<a id="tld_galloc_dim1"></a><a id="tld_galloc_dim2"></a>

### `tld_galloc_dim1`, `tld_galloc_dim2`

```c
TLD_API int tld_galloc_dim1(void *ptr, uint32_t *d);
TLD_API int tld_galloc_dim2(void *ptr, uint32_t *d);
```

Dimensions of a galloc block: rows (n) into *d, and columns (k, 0 for a 1D array)
into *d. FAIL if ptr is NULL. Only valid for memory from galloc.

<a id="mod-string"></a>

## string

`src/string/tld-string.h`: Tld_strbuf, a growable NUL-terminated byte buffer (append, prepend, copy). Inspired by the rayfork str code by Sas Luca.

<a id="tld_strbuf"></a>

### `tld_strbuf`

```c
typedef struct tld_strbuf {
        uint8_t* str;
        int32_t len;
        int32_t alloc_len;
} tld_strbuf;
```

A growable byte buffer: len bytes at str, always followed by a NUL, in alloc_len
bytes. TLD_STR(b) gives it as char *. Appending may move str, so do not keep that
pointer across changes. Create with tld_strbuf_alloc, free with tld_strbuf_free.
A buffer holds at most INT32_MAX - 1 bytes; an append that would pass that fails
with an error and leaves the buffer unchanged.

<a id="TLD_STR"></a><a id="TLD_STRLEN"></a>

### `TLD_STR`, `TLD_STRLEN`

```c
#define TLD_STR(X) ((char*)(X)->str)
#define TLD_STRLEN(X) (X)->len
```

TLD_STR(b): the contents of the tld_strbuf * b as char *; TLD_STRLEN(b): its length in
bytes.

<a id="tld_strbuf_alloc"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_alloc`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_alloc(tld_strbuf **buffer, int size);
```

A new empty buffer in *buffer with size bytes reserved (0 means 1024; size < 0 is an
error). It grows as needed. Free with tld_strbuf_free.

<a id="tld_strbuf_free"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_strbuf_free(tld_strbuf *b);
```

Free a buffer; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_strbuf_clear"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_clear`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_clear(tld_strbuf *b);
```

Empty the buffer (len 0); the memory is kept.

<a id="tld_strbuf_copy"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_copy`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_copy(tld_strbuf *t, tld_strbuf *s);
```

Replace the contents of t with a copy of s; t grows as needed.

<a id="tld_strbuf_append"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_append`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_append(tld_strbuf *b, const char *content);
```

Append the NUL-terminated string content to b; b grows as needed.

<a id="tld_strbuf_append_char"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_append_char`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_append_char(tld_strbuf *b, char c);
```

Append the single character c to b.

<a id="tld_strbuf_prepend"></a>

### `tld_strbuf_prepend`

```c
TLD_API int tld_strbuf_prepend(tld_strbuf *b, const char *content);
```

Insert the NUL-terminated string content at the start of b.

## path

`src/path/tld-path.h`: File and directory checks, absolute paths, file and directory names of a path, and capturing the command line.

<a id="tld_path_exists"></a>

### `tld_path_exists`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_exists(const char* name);
```

OK if name exists (a file, directory or anything else stat() sees), FAIL otherwise,
without a message. Test with == OK.

<a id="tld_path_is_dir"></a>

### `tld_path_is_dir`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_is_dir(const char *name);
```

OK if name is a directory that can be opened; otherwise prints an error and returns
FAIL.

<a id="tld_path_mkdir"></a>

### `tld_path_mkdir`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_mkdir(char *dir);
```

Create the directory dir (mode 0700; its parent must exist). OK when it was created
or already exists as a directory (with a warning); FAIL otherwise.

<a id="tld_path_full"></a>

### `tld_path_full`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_full(tld_strbuf **full, char *filename);
```

The absolute, symlink-free path of the existing file filename into *full. A non-NULL
*full is cleared and reused; otherwise a buffer is allocated (free with
tld_strbuf_free). FAIL when the file does not exist.

<a id="tld_cmdline_capture"></a>

### `tld_cmdline_capture`

```c
TLD_API int tld_cmdline_capture(tld_strbuf **cmdline, const int argc, char *const argv[]);
```

Append argv[0] .. argv[argc - 1], each followed by a space, to *cmdline (allocated when
NULL; free with tld_strbuf_free). For recording how a program was run.

<a id="tld_path_filename"></a>

### `tld_path_filename`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_filename(char* path, char** out);
```

A new string in *out (free with MFREE or free) with the part of path after the last
'/'. FAIL when that part is empty (path is empty or ends in '/').

<a id="tld_path_dirname"></a>

### `tld_path_dirname`

```c
TLD_API int tld_path_dirname(char* path, char** out);
```

A new string in *out (free with MFREE or free) with the part of path before the last
'/' ("/" for "/name"). FAIL when path contains no '/'.

## timing

`src/timing/tld-timing.h`: One global wall-clock stopwatch that prints elapsed seconds to stdout.

<a id="TLD_START_TIMER"></a><a id="TLD_END_TIMER"></a>

### `TLD_START_TIMER`, `TLD_END_TIMER`

```c
#define TLD_START_TIMER tld__timer(0);
#define TLD_END_TIMER tld__timer(1);
```

Complete statements (they include the semicolon): TLD_START_TIMER starts the
stopwatch, TLD_END_TIMER prints the elapsed time (tld__timer(0) / (1)).

## bitfield

`src/bitfield/tld-bitfield.h`: Fixed-length bit sets with set, get and clear, OR, copy and (masked) Hamming distance.

<a id="tld_bitfield"></a>

### `tld_bitfield`

```c
typedef struct {
        uint64_t* m;
        int32_t len;
        int32_t alloc_len;
} tld_bitfield;
```

A set of len bits, stored in alloc_len 64-bit words m. Create with tld_bitfield_alloc,
free with tld_bitfield_free.

<a id="tld_bitfield_alloc"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_alloc`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_alloc(tld_bitfield **bit_f, int32_t size);
```

A new bitfield of size bits, all 0, in *bit_f. Free with tld_bitfield_free.

<a id="tld_bitfield_free"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_bitfield_free(tld_bitfield *b);
```

Free a bitfield; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_bitfield_reset"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_reset`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_reset(tld_bitfield *b);
```

Clear every bit.

<a id="tld_bitfield_set"></a><a id="tld_bitfield_get"></a><a id="tld_bitfield_clear"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_set`, `tld_bitfield_get`, `tld_bitfield_clear`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_set(tld_bitfield *b, int32_t index);
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_get(tld_bitfield *b, int32_t index, uint8_t* bit);
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_clear(tld_bitfield *b, int32_t index);
```

Set bit index to 1, read it into *bit (0 or 1), or clear it to 0. FAIL, without a
message, when index is outside [0, len).

<a id="tld_bitfield_copy"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_copy`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_copy(tld_bitfield *dst, tld_bitfield *src);
```

Copy the bits of src into dst; both must have the same length.

<a id="tld_bitfield_or"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_or`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_or(tld_bitfield *b1, tld_bitfield *b2,tld_bitfield* ret);
```

ret = b1 | b2, bit by bit; all three must have the same length.

<a id="tld_bitfield_hamming"></a>

### `tld_bitfield_hamming`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_bitfield_hamming(tld_bitfield *b1, tld_bitfield *b2,tld_bitfield *mask, int32_t *dist);
```

The number of positions at which b1 and b2 differ into *dist, counting only positions
set in mask (NULL: all). The bitfields (and mask) must have the same length.

<a id="mod-hash"></a>

## hash

`src/hash/tld-hash.h`: A string-to-string hash map (FNV-1a, chaining, grows automatically). Keys and values are copied in; pointers handed out are borrowed from the map. Not locked: one thread at a time per map.

<a id="tld_hash"></a>

### `tld_hash`

```c
typedef struct tld_hash tld_hash;
```

Opaque string-to-string map. Create with tld_hash_alloc (or let tld_hash_add create
it), free with tld_hash_free.

<a id="tld_hash_alloc"></a>

### `tld_hash_alloc`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_alloc(tld_hash **hash, int size);
```

Allocate an empty map in *hash with more than size buckets (a prime); it grows when
the entries outnumber 3/4 of the buckets. Free with tld_hash_free.

<a id="tld_hash_free"></a>

### `tld_hash_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_hash_free(tld_hash *h);
```

Free the map and every key and value; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_hash_add"></a>

### `tld_hash_add`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_add(tld_hash **hash, const char *key, const char *val);
```

Insert key -> val (both copied), replacing the value if key exists. When *hash is NULL
a map is allocated first and stored in *hash.

<a id="tld_hash_get"></a>

### `tld_hash_get`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_get(tld_hash *h, const char *key, const char **val);
```

Look up key: *val points to the stored value (borrowed and read-only: do not write
to it or free it; valid until the entry changes or the map is freed). Returns FAIL, without a message, and sets *val to NULL when key
is absent.

<a id="tld_hash_del"></a>

### `tld_hash_del`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_del(tld_hash *h, const char *key);
```

Remove key. Returns FAIL, without a message, when key is absent.

<a id="tld_hash_rename"></a>

### `tld_hash_rename`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_rename(tld_hash *h, const char *key, const char *new_key);
```

Move the value stored under key to new_key (replacing any value there). Returns FAIL
when key is absent.

<a id="tld_hash_iter_init"></a>

### `tld_hash_iter_init`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_iter_init(tld_hash *h);
```

Start iterating over the map (entries come in no particular order).

<a id="tld_hash_iter_next"></a>

### `tld_hash_iter_next`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_hash_iter_next(tld_hash* h, const char **key, const char **value);
```

Next entry: *key and *value point into the map (borrowed and read-only). Returns FAIL, without a
message, when there are no more entries. Do not add or delete while iterating.

```c
const char *k, *v;
RUN(tld_hash_iter_init(h));
while(tld_hash_iter_next(h, &k, &v) == OK){ ... }
```

<a id="mod-json-types"></a>

## json types

`src/json/tld-json_struct.h`: The JSON tree. An object (tld_json_obj) maps n keys to values, an array (tld_json_arr) holds n values, and each value (tld_json_val) is tagged with its tld_json_type. Containers own everything below them.

<a id="tld_json_type"></a>

### `tld_json_type`

```c
typedef enum tld_json_type {
        TLD_JSON_OBJ,
        TLD_JSON_ARR,
        TLD_JSON_STR,
        TLD_JSON_DBL,
        TLD_JSON_INT,
        TLD_JSON_BOOL_TRUE,
        TLD_JSON_BOOL_FALSE,
        TLD_JSON_NULL
} tld_json_type;
```

Type tag of a tld_json_val. JSON null is TLD_JSON_NULL.

<a id="tld_json_val"></a>

### `tld_json_val`

```c
typedef struct tld_json_val{
        tld_json_type type;
        union{
                tld_json_obj* obj;
                tld_json_arr* arr;
                tld_strbuf* str;
                double d_num;
                int32_t i_num;
                int8_t  b_num;
        } value;
} tld_json_val;
```

One JSON value. type selects the member of value: obj, arr, str, d_num (TLD_JSON_DBL),
i_num (TLD_JSON_INT) or b_num (the two BOOL types). Integers outside int32_t are stored
as TLD_JSON_DBL.

<a id="tld_json_obj"></a>

### `tld_json_obj`

```c
typedef struct tld_json_obj{
        tld_strbuf** key;
        tld_json_val** v;
        int n;
        int n_alloc;

} tld_json_obj;
```

A JSON object: key[i] maps to v[i] for i < n, in document order (duplicate keys are
kept); n_alloc slots exist. Made by tld_json_parse, TLD_JSON_OBJECT or tld_json_obj_alloc;
freed with tld_json_obj_free.

<a id="tld_json_arr"></a>

### `tld_json_arr`

```c
typedef struct tld_json_arr {
        tld_json_val** v;
        int read_head;
        int n;
        int n_alloc;
} tld_json_arr;
```

A JSON array of n values v[0..n-1] (read_head is unused). Made by TLD_JSON_ARRAY or
tld_json_arr_alloc; freed with tld_json_arr_free.

<a id="tld_json_decoration"></a>

### `tld_json_decoration`

```c
typedef struct {
        char* key;
        void* value;
        /* VAL_STRING guesses the type from the text (TLD_JAUTO); the values after
           VAL_ARR are the typed decorations TLD_JSTR, TLD_JNUM, TLD_JINT, TLD_JBOOL, TLD_JNULL. */
        enum { VAL_STRING, VAL_OBJ, VAL_ARR, VAL_JSTR, VAL_NUM, VAL_INT, VAL_BOOL, VAL_NULL } type;
} tld_json_decoration;
```

One entry for TLD_JSON_OBJECT / TLD_JSON_ARRAY, made by TLD_JAUTO, TLD_JOBJ, TLD_JARR, TLD_JSTR, TLD_JNUM, TLD_JINT, TLD_JBOOL or
TLD_JNULL.

<a id="mod-json-memory"></a>

## json memory

`src/json/tld-json_mem.h`: Allocate, deep-copy and free JSON objects, arrays and values.

<a id="tld_json_obj_alloc"></a>

### `tld_json_obj_alloc`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_json_obj_alloc(tld_json_obj **obj);
```

A new empty object in *obj. Free with tld_json_obj_free.

<a id="tld_json_obj_free"></a>

### `tld_json_obj_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_json_obj_free(tld_json_obj *n);
```

Free an object with all its keys and values; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_json_obj_copy"></a>

### `tld_json_obj_copy`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_json_obj_copy(tld_json_obj **target, tld_json_obj *s);
```

Deep copy of the object s into a new object in *target (free with tld_json_obj_free).

<a id="tld_json_arr_alloc"></a>

### `tld_json_arr_alloc`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_json_arr_alloc(tld_json_arr **arr);
```

A new empty array in *arr. Free with tld_json_arr_free.

<a id="tld_json_arr_free"></a>

### `tld_json_arr_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_json_arr_free(tld_json_arr *n);
```

Free an array with all its values; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_json_arr_copy"></a>

### `tld_json_arr_copy`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_json_arr_copy(tld_json_arr **t, tld_json_arr *s);
```

Deep copy of the array s into a new array in *t (free with tld_json_arr_free).

<a id="tld_json_val_alloc"></a>

### `tld_json_val_alloc`

```c
TLD_API   int tld_json_val_alloc(tld_json_val **node);
```

A new value of type TLD_JSON_NULL (null) in *node. Free with tld_json_val_free.

<a id="tld_json_val_free"></a>

### `tld_json_val_free`

```c
TLD_API  void tld_json_val_free(tld_json_val *n);
```

Free a value and everything it owns; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_json_val_copy"></a>

### `tld_json_val_copy`

```c
TLD_API   int tld_json_val_copy(tld_json_val *t, tld_json_val *s);
```

Deep copy s into t. Whatever t held is released first, so t may change type; s may
live inside t.

<a id="mod-json"></a>

## json

`src/json/tld-json.h`: Parse JSON text into a tree (tld_json_parse), build trees with TLD_JSON_OBJECT and TLD_JSON_ARRAY, read values by path (tld_json_get_*), search and update, and write JSON text (tld_json_dump).

<a id="tld_json_parse"></a>

### `tld_json_parse`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_json_parse(tld_strbuf *t, tld_json_obj **out);
```

Parse the JSON text in t (standard JSON, nesting up to 512 levels) into a new object in
*out; free it with tld_json_obj_free. A top-level array becomes the single entry of
an object, under the key "Top Level Arr". Invalid JSON prints an error naming the byte
offset and returns FAIL.

<a id="tld_json_search"></a>

### `tld_json_search`

```c
TLD_API int tld_json_search(tld_json_obj *n, char *key, tld_json_obj **ret);
```

Collect deep copies of every value stored under key, at any depth, into a new object
in *ret (entries named key, in document order; free with tld_json_obj_free). OK with
an empty result when nothing matches.

<a id="tld_json_get_str"></a><a id="tld_json_get_num"></a><a id="tld_json_get_int"></a><a id="tld_json_get_bool"></a><a id="tld_json_get_obj"></a><a id="tld_json_get_arr"></a>

### `tld_json_get_str`, `tld_json_get_num`, `tld_json_get_int`, `tld_json_get_bool`, `tld_json_get_obj`, `tld_json_get_arr`

```c
TLD_API int tld_json_get_str(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, const char **out);
TLD_API int tld_json_get_num(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, double *out);
TLD_API int tld_json_get_int(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, int64_t *out);
TLD_API int tld_json_get_bool(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, int *out);
TLD_API int tld_json_get_obj(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, tld_json_obj **out);
TLD_API int tld_json_get_arr(tld_json_obj *obj, const char *path, tld_json_arr **out);
```

Path getters. A path is dot-separated keys with [i] for array elements,
e.g. "message.content", "embeddings[0]", "models[2].name". tld_json_parse
stores a top-level array under the key "Top Level Arr"; address it as
"Top Level Arr[0]..." or simply "[0]...". Keys containing '.' or '[' cannot
be addressed. All return OK, or FAIL (leaving *out unchanged) when the path
does not exist or the value has another type. Strings, objects and arrays
are borrowed from the tree. get_num accepts integers; get_int accepts
integral doubles inside the int64_t range. JSON null has type
TLD_JSON_NULL and fails every getter. An empty path in get_obj returns
obj itself. out may be NULL to test whether the path exists.

<a id="tld_json_set_val"></a>

### `tld_json_set_val`

```c
TLD_API int tld_json_set_val(tld_json_obj *n, char *key, tld_json_val *v);
```

Set the value at a path to a deep copy of v. key is a path in the syntax of the
tld_json_get_* getters ("name", "a.b", "list[2].id", "[0]" for a parsed top-level
array). Everything before the last step must exist. The last step may name a key
that is missing (it is added at the end of its object) or the index one past the
end of an array (v is appended). An existing value is replaced, even by one of
another type, and v may be part of n. Returns FAIL for a missing parent, an index
further past the end, or no memory. Keys containing '.' or '[' cannot be addressed.

<a id="TLD_JAUTO"></a><a id="TLD_JOBJ"></a><a id="TLD_JARR"></a>

### `TLD_JAUTO`, `TLD_JOBJ`, `TLD_JARR`

```c
#define TLD_JAUTO(k,v) ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_STRING, .value = (void*)(v)})
#define TLD_JOBJ(k,v) ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_OBJ, .value = (void*)(v)})
#define TLD_JARR(k,v) ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_ARR, .value = (void*)(v)})
```

Entries for TLD_JSON_OBJECT / TLD_JSON_ARRAY. TLD_JAUTO(k, s): the string s, with its type guessed from
the text: "12" becomes an integer, "0.2" a number, true/false (also True, TRUE, ...) a
boolean, anything else a string. TLD_JOBJ(k, o) / TLD_JARR(k, a): a nested tld_json_obj * /
tld_json_arr *, which the new container takes over (do not free it yourself), also
when the build fails. A TLD_JAUTO or TLD_JSTR entry whose string is NULL is skipped; a TLD_JOBJ or TLD_JARR
entry whose value is NULL makes the build fail, since a nested TLD_JSON_OBJECT / TLD_JSON_ARRAY
returns NULL only when it failed. Arrays ignore the key; pass NULL.

<a id="TLD_JSTR"></a><a id="TLD_JNUM"></a><a id="TLD_JINT"></a><a id="TLD_JBOOL"></a><a id="TLD_JNULL"></a>

### `TLD_JSTR`, `TLD_JNUM`, `TLD_JINT`, `TLD_JBOOL`, `TLD_JNULL`

```c
#define TLD_JSTR(k,v)  ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_JSTR, .value = (void*)(v)})
#define TLD_JNUM(k,v)  ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_NUM,  .value = (void*)&(double){(v)}})
#define TLD_JINT(k,v)  ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_INT,  .value = (void*)&(long){(v)}})
#define TLD_JBOOL(k,v) ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_BOOL, .value = (void*)&(int){(v)}})
#define TLD_JNULL(k)   ((tld_json_decoration){.key =(char*)k, .type = VAL_NULL, .value = (void*)""})
```

Typed decorations. TLD_JAUTO above guesses the type from the text ("0.2" becomes
a number); these do not. TLD_JSTR(k,s) is always a string, TLD_JNUM(k,d) a number
(non-finite values are written as null), TLD_JINT(k,l) an integer (values
outside int32_t are stored as double), TLD_JBOOL(k,b) true/false, TLD_JNULL(k) null.
A NULL string in TLD_JSTR skips the entry, like TLD_JAUTO.

<a id="TLD_JSON_OBJECT"></a><a id="TLD_JSON_ARRAY"></a>

### `TLD_JSON_OBJECT`, `TLD_JSON_ARRAY`

```c
#define TLD_JSON_OBJECT(...) tld__json_obj_build(NULL, (tld_json_decoration[]){__VA_ARGS__}, \
                                            sizeof((tld_json_decoration[]){__VA_ARGS__})/sizeof(tld_json_decoration))
#define TLD_JSON_ARRAY(...) tld__json_arr_build(NULL, (tld_json_decoration[]){__VA_ARGS__}, \
                                            sizeof((tld_json_decoration[]){__VA_ARGS__})/sizeof(tld_json_decoration))
```

TLD_JSON_OBJECT(entry, ...): a new tld_json_obj * holding the entries in order; TLD_JSON_ARRAY(...)
a new tld_json_arr *. NULL (with an error printed) when an entry cannot be added: out
of memory, or a TLD_JOBJ/TLD_JARR entry holding NULL. The containers passed in with TLD_JOBJ/TLD_JARR are then
freed too. Free the result with tld_json_obj_free / tld_json_arr_free.

```c
tld_json_obj *o = TLD_JSON_OBJECT(TLD_JSTR("name", "x"), TLD_JINT("n", 3),
                           TLD_JARR("v", TLD_JSON_ARRAY(TLD_JNUM(NULL, 0.5), TLD_JNUM(NULL, 2))));
```

<a id="tld_json_dump"></a><a id="tld_json_dump_arr"></a>

### `tld_json_dump`, `tld_json_dump_arr`

```c
TLD_API int tld_json_dump(tld_json_obj *n, tld_strbuf *b,int indent);
TLD_API int tld_json_dump_arr(tld_json_arr *n, tld_strbuf *b, int indent);
```

Append n as JSON text to b (b is not cleared): 4 spaces of indentation per level on
top of indent (pass 0), strings escaped, doubles with the fewest of 15 to 17 significant
digits that read back exactly, inf/nan as null. A NULL n appends nothing.

<a id="mod-template"></a>

## template

`src/template/tld-template.h`: Fill {{name}} placeholders and {{IF name}}...{{ELSE}}...{{ENDIF}} blocks in text from a tld_hash of names to values.

<a id="tld_template_apply"></a>

### `tld_template_apply`

```c
TLD_API int tld_template_apply(tld_strbuf *txt, tld_hash *map);
```

Render the template in txt in place. {{name}} becomes map's value for name (nothing
when absent); {{IF name}}A{{ELSE}}B{{ENDIF}} keeps A when name has a non-empty value
and B otherwise (ELSE is optional; IFs nest). The text between the braces is the key
as written (no trimming, 1 to 63 characters). map must not be NULL. A malformed
template (unclosed IF or tag, ELSE or ENDIF without IF, an empty {{}}, an IF with no
name) prints the reason with its byte offset and returns FAIL with txt unchanged.

```c
tld_hash *m = NULL;
RUN(tld_hash_add(&m, "who", "world"));
RUN(tld_strbuf_append(txt, "Hello {{who}}{{IF excl}}!{{ENDIF}}"));
RUN(tld_template_apply(txt, m));        // txt is now "Hello world"
```

<a id="tld_template_vars"></a>

### `tld_template_vars`

```c
TLD_API int tld_template_vars(tld_strbuf *txt, tld_hash **hash);
```

A new map in *hash (free with tld_hash_free) whose keys are the variable names used
in txt, from {{name}} and {{IF name}}, each mapped to itself.

<a id="mod-rng"></a>

## rng

`src/rng/tld-rng.h`: The xoshiro256** random number generator (seedable, and splittable for threads) with uniform, integer, Gaussian and gamma draws, plus alias-table sampling from a discrete distribution. A generator is not locked: use one per thread.

<a id="tld_rng"></a>

### `tld_rng`

```c
typedef struct tld_rng tld_rng;
```

Opaque generator state. Create with tld_rng_alloc or tld_rng_split, free with
tld_rng_free.

<a id="tld_rng_dist"></a>

### `tld_rng_dist`

```c
struct tld_rng_dist;
```

Opaque alias table for sampling from a discrete distribution (tl_random_sdist_*).

<a id="tld_rng_alloc"></a>

### `tld_rng_alloc`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_alloc(struct tld_rng **rng, uint64_t seed);
```

Allocate a generator in *rng seeded with seed; the same seed gives the same sequence.
seed 0 picks a seed from /dev/urandom, mixed with the time, the process id and a
counter, so every generator made with seed 0 has its own stream, also across jobs
started at the same moment. Free with tld_rng_free.

<a id="tld_rng_split"></a>

### `tld_rng_split`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_split(struct tld_rng** target, struct tld_rng* rng);
```

Allocate a generator for another thread in *target: it continues rng's current
stream, and rng itself jumps 2^128 draws ahead, so the two streams never overlap.
Free with tld_rng_free.

<a id="tld_rng_set_seed"></a>

### `tld_rng_set_seed`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_set_seed(struct tld_rng *s, uint64_t seed);
```

Reseed an existing generator (seed is used as given, 0 included) and drop any cached
Gaussian deviate.

<a id="tld_rng_free"></a>

### `tld_rng_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_rng_free(struct tld_rng* rng);
```

Free a generator; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_rng_double"></a>

### `tld_rng_double`

```c
TLD_API double tld_rng_double(struct tld_rng* rng);
```

Uniform double on the open interval (0, 1): never exactly 0 or 1.

<a id="tld_rng_gaussian"></a>

### `tld_rng_gaussian`

```c
TLD_API double tld_rng_gaussian(struct tld_rng* rng, double mu, double sigma);
```

Normal deviate with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (Box-Muller; values are made
in pairs and every other call returns the cached second one).

<a id="tld_rng_gamma"></a>

### `tld_rng_gamma`

```c
TLD_API double tld_rng_gamma(struct tld_rng* rng, double shape, double scale);
```

Gamma deviate with the given shape (> 0, not checked) and scale; mean shape * scale.

<a id="tld_rng_int"></a>

### `tld_rng_int`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_int(struct tld_rng* rng,int a);
```

Uniform integer in [0, a), without modulo bias; 0 when a <= 1.

<a id="tld_rng_dist_alloc"></a>

### `tld_rng_dist_alloc`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_dist_alloc(struct tld_rng_dist** dist,double* w, int n,int seed);
```

Build in *tld_rng_dist an alias table that samples index i in [0, n) with probability
w[i] / sum(w). Weights must be >= 0 with a finite, positive sum. The table owns its
own generator seeded with seed (0 = arbitrary). Free with tld_rng_dist_free.

<a id="tld_rng_dist_sample"></a>

### `tld_rng_dist_sample`

```c
TLD_API int tld_rng_dist_sample(struct tld_rng_dist* d);
```

One sample from the table: an index in [0, n).

<a id="tld_rng_dist_free"></a>

### `tld_rng_dist_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_rng_dist_free(struct tld_rng_dist* d);
```

Free an alias table and its generator; NULL is ignored.

<a id="mod-sort"></a>

## sort

`src/sort/tld-sort.h`: In-place sorting of arrays of char, int8_t..int64_t, uint8_t..uint64_t, float and double, ascending or descending; TLD_SORT_ASC and TLD_SORT_DESC pick the function from the array's type.

<a id="tld_sort_desc_char"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_char"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_int8_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_int8_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_uint8_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_uint8_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_int16_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_int16_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_uint16_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_uint16_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_int32_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_int32_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_uint32_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_uint32_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_int64_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_int64_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_uint64_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_uint64_t"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_float"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_float"></a><a id="tld_sort_desc_double"></a><a id="tld_sort_asc_double"></a>

### `tld_sort_desc_<type>`, `tld_sort_asc_<type>`

```c
int tld_sort_desc_char(char *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_char(char* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_int8_t(int8_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_int8_t(int8_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_uint8_t(uint8_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_uint8_t(uint8_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_int16_t(int16_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_int16_t(int16_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_uint16_t(uint16_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_uint16_t(uint16_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_int32_t(int32_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_int32_t(int32_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_uint32_t(uint32_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_uint32_t(uint32_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_int64_t(int64_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_int64_t(int64_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_uint64_t(uint64_t *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_uint64_t(uint64_t* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_float(float *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_float(float* a, int len);
int tld_sort_desc_double(double *a, int len);
int tld_sort_asc_double(double* a, int len);
```

Sort len elements of a in place, descending (sort_desc_*) or ascending (sort_asc_*),
with qsort (not stable). Always OK. Arrays holding NaN have no defined order.

<a id="TLD_SORT_DESC"></a>

### `TLD_SORT_DESC`

```c
#define TLD_SORT_DESC(A,N) ...
```

TLD_SORT_DESC(a, len): sort_desc_<type>(a, len) for a's element type.

<a id="TLD_SORT_ASC"></a>

### `TLD_SORT_ASC`

```c
#define TLD_SORT_ASC(A,N) ...
```

TLD_SORT_ASC(a, len): sort_asc_<type>(a, len) for a's element type.

<a id="mod-shuffle"></a>

## shuffle

`src/shuffle/tld-shuffle.h`: Uniform random permutation (Fisher-Yates) in place of arrays of char, int8_t..int64_t, uint8_t..uint64_t, float and double; TLD_SHUFFLE picks the function from the array's type.

<a id="tld_shuffle_char"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_int8_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_uint8_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_int16_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_uint16_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_int32_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_uint32_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_int64_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_uint64_t"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_float"></a><a id="tld_shuffle_double"></a>

### `tld_shuffle_<type>`

```c
int tld_shuffle_char(char *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_int8_t(int8_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_uint8_t(uint8_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_int16_t(int16_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_uint16_t(uint16_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_int32_t(int32_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_uint32_t(uint32_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_int64_t(int64_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_uint64_t(uint64_t *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_float(float *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
int tld_shuffle_double(double *a, int len, struct tld_rng* rng);
```

Shuffle len elements of a in place, drawing from rng (see tld_rng_alloc). Always OK.

<a id="TLD_SHUFFLE"></a>

### `TLD_SHUFFLE`

```c
#define TLD_SHUFFLE(A,N,R) ...
```

TLD_SHUFFLE(a, len, rng): tld_shuffle_<type>(a, len, rng) for a's element type.

<a id="mod-stats"></a>

## stats

`src/stats/tld-stats.h`: Descriptive statistics of double arrays (mean, variance, covariance, Pearson correlation, Shannon entropy, standardising), the sigmoid, the normal density and Gaussian kernel density estimates. Results come back through the last argument.

<a id="tld_shannon"></a>

### `tld_shannon`

```c
TLD_API int tld_shannon(double *vec, int n, double *entropy);
```

Shannon entropy in bits of the distribution vec[i] / sum(vec) (n >= 1, every
vec[i] >= 0); 0 when all values are 0.

<a id="tld_mean"></a>

### `tld_mean`

```c
TLD_API int tld_mean(double *vec, int n, double *mean);
```

Arithmetic mean of n >= 1 values.

<a id="tld_pop_variance"></a><a id="tld_sample_variance"></a>

### `tld_pop_variance`, `tld_sample_variance`

```c
TLD_API int tld_pop_variance(double *vec, int n, double *variance);
TLD_API int tld_sample_variance(double *vec, int n, double *variance);
```

Variance dividing by n (population, n >= 1) or by n - 1 (sample, n >= 2).

<a id="tld_standardise"></a>

### `tld_standardise`

```c
TLD_API int tld_standardise(double *vec, int n, double *mean, double *stdev);
```

Standardise vec in place to (x - mean) / sd, with the sample standard deviation;
the mean and sd used come back in *mean and *stdev. FAIL when sd is 0 or n < 2.

<a id="tld_sample_covariance"></a><a id="tld_pop_covariance"></a>

### `tld_sample_covariance`, `tld_pop_covariance`

```c
TLD_API int tld_sample_covariance(double *vec_a, double *vec_b, int n, double *cov);
TLD_API int tld_pop_covariance(double *vec_a, double *vec_b, int n, double *cov);
```

Covariance of two arrays of n values, dividing by n - 1 (sample, n >= 2) or by n
(population).

<a id="tld_pearson_corr"></a>

### `tld_pearson_corr`

```c
TLD_API int tld_pearson_corr(double *vec_a, double *vec_b, int n, double *corr);
```

Pearson correlation of two arrays of n values, in [-1, 1]; 0 when either array is
constant.

<a id="tld_sigmoid"></a><a id="tld_sigmoid_safe"></a>

### `tld_sigmoid`, `tld_sigmoid_safe`

```c
TLD_API int tld_sigmoid(double x, double *out);
TLD_API int tld_sigmoid_safe(double x, double *out);
```

1 / (1 + exp(-x)), computed without overflow. tld_sigmoid fails (FAIL) for an
infinite or NaN x; tld_sigmoid_safe never fails: NaN gives NaN, +inf 1, -inf 0.

<a id="tld_normal_pdf"></a>

### `tld_normal_pdf`

```c
TLD_API int tld_normal_pdf(double x, double mu, double sigma, double* p);
```

Density at x of the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation
sigma (> 0).

<a id="tld_kde_pdf"></a>

### `tld_kde_pdf`

```c
TLD_API int tld_kde_pdf(double *data, int data_len, int n_steps, double ***out);
```

Gaussian kernel density estimate of data[0..data_len-1], bandwidth sd * (3n/4)^(-1/5),
evaluated at the centres of n_steps equal bins spanning [min, max] of the data. *out
is a new n_steps x 2 galloc matrix, out[i][0] = x and out[i][1] = density; free with
gfree.

<a id="tld_kde_count_pdf"></a>

### `tld_kde_count_pdf`

```c
TLD_API int tld_kde_count_pdf(double *data,double* cnt, int data_len, double*** out);
```

Weighted kernel density estimate: value data[i] seen cnt[i] (>= 0) times. The density
is evaluated at each data[i]: *out is a new data_len x 2 galloc matrix, out[i][0] =
data[i] and out[i][1] = density; free with gfree.

<a id="mod-quantile"></a>

## quantile

`src/stats/tld-quantile.h`: Quantile normalisation of the columns of a matrix.

<a id="tld_quantile_normalise"></a>

### `tld_quantile_normalise`

```c
TLD_API int tld_quantile_normalise(double** data, int n, int m);
```

Quantile-normalise, in place, the m columns of the n x m matrix data (data[i][j] is
row i, column j; e.g. from galloc(&data, n, m)). Afterwards every column has the same
distribution: the mean over columns of the sorted values. Tied values in a column
share the mean of their positions. NaN is an error.

<a id="mod-auc"></a>

## auc

`src/stats/tld-auc.h`: Area under the ROC curve, and the best score threshold, for 0/1 labels and real-valued scores.

<a id="tld_auc"></a>

### `tld_auc`

```c
TLD_API int tld_auc(double *Y, double *Y_hat, int n, double *t, double *ret);
```

ROC analysis of n samples: Y[i] is the label (1.0 positive; any other value in [0, 1]
negative), Y_hat[i] the score (higher means more likely positive; no NaN). Both
classes must occur. *ret is the AUC (trapezoids, tied scores form one step) and *t
the score nearest the (0, 1) corner of the curve: call Y_hat >= *t positive.

<a id="tld_auc_calculate"></a><a id="tld_auc_best_threshold"></a>

### `tld_auc_calculate`, `tld_auc_best_threshold`

```c
TLD_API int tld_auc_calculate(double *Y, double *Y_hat, int n, double *ret);
TLD_API int tld_auc_best_threshold(double *Y, double *Y_hat, int n, double *best_threshold);
```

tld_auc giving only the AUC (tld_auc_calculate) or only the threshold
(tld_auc_best_threshold).

<a id="mod-logsum"></a>

## logsum

`src/logsum/tld-logsum.h`: Arithmetic on probabilities stored as logarithms (log-sum-exp via a lookup table) and tolerant floating-point equality.

<a id="tld_logsum_init"></a>

### `tld_logsum_init`

```c
TLD_API void tld_logsum_init(void);
```

Fill logsum's lookup table. Optional (logsum does it on first use); thread-safe.

<a id="tld_logsum"></a>

### `tld_logsum`

```c
TLD_API float tld_logsum(const float a,const float b);
```

log(exp(a) + exp(b)) for log-space values, from a table with steps of 0.001. NaN if
either is NaN; -INFINITY acts as log(0); returns max(a, b) when they differ by 15.7 or
more.

<a id="tld_nearly_equal_float"></a><a id="tld_nearly_equal_double"></a>

### `tld_nearly_equal_float`, `tld_nearly_equal_double`

```c
TLD_API int tld_nearly_equal_float(float a, float b);
TLD_API int tld_nearly_equal_double(double a, double b);
```

1 if a and b are equal up to a relative difference of FLT_EPSILON / DBL_EPSILON (an
absolute one when either is 0 or both are tiny), else 0.

<a id="TLD_NEARLY_EQUAL"></a>

### `TLD_NEARLY_EQUAL`

```c
#define TLD_NEARLY_EQUAL(X,Y) _Generic((X),                        \
                                float: tld_nearly_equal_float,  \
                                double: tld_nearly_equal_double \
                )(X,Y)
```

TLD_NEARLY_EQUAL(X, Y): tld_nearly_equal_float or tld_nearly_equal_double, chosen by the type of X
(float or double only).

<a id="mod-kdtree"></a>

## kdtree

`src/kdtree/tld-kdtree.h`: A k-d tree of double vectors with caller-chosen ids for nearest-neighbour search (squared Euclidean distance by default); points can be built in bulk or inserted one at a time. Not locked: changing a tree (alloc, build, insert, rebalance, reset) needs it to itself, but searches only read it and may run at the same time.

<a id="tld_kdtree_node"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_node`

```c
typedef struct tld_kdtree_node {
        double* p;
        struct tld_kdtree_node* left;
        struct tld_kdtree_node* right;
        uint32_t id;
        int n;
} tld_kdtree_node;
```

A tree node: p is the point (n doubles, owned by the tree), id the caller's id.

<a id="tld_kdtree"></a>

### `tld_kdtree`

```c
typedef struct tld_kdtree {
        tld_kdtree_node* root;
        struct tld__kdyard* yard;
        int(*fptr_cmp)(double*, double*, int, double*);
        int(*fptr_plane)(double*, double*, int, double);
        int rebalance_at;
        int n_step;
        int depth;
        int max_depth;
        int min_depth;
        int vec_len;
} tld_kdtree;
```

A k-d tree; create with tld_kdtree_alloc, free with tld_kdtree_free. Fields a caller may set:
fptr_cmp (distance, default tld_kdtree_dist_euclidean) with the matching fptr_plane (default
tld_kdtree_plane_euclidean), and rebalance_at (insertions between balance checks, default
10000). The rest is internal.

<a id="tld_kdtree_alloc"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_alloc`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_alloc(tld_kdtree **tree, int size);
```

Allocate in *tree an empty tree for points of size (> 0) dimensions, using squared
Euclidean distance. Storage grows as points are added. Free with tld_kdtree_free.

<a id="tld_kdtree_free"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_kdtree_free(tld_kdtree *t);
```

Free the tree and all its points; NULL is ignored.

<a id="tld_kdtree_reset"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_reset`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_reset(tld_kdtree *t);
```

Remove every point and keep the memory for reuse.

<a id="tld_kdtree_build"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_build`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_build(tld_kdtree *t, double **x,uint32_t* ids, int n, int size);
```

Add n points x[i] of size doubles (size <= the length given to tld_kdtree_alloc) with
ids[i] and rebuild the tree balanced. The points are copied; x and ids are not
changed. On failure (no memory) the tree is unchanged.

<a id="tld_kdtree_insert"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_insert`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_insert(tld_kdtree* t, double *x,uint32_t id, int size);
```

Insert one point x of size doubles with id (copied). Every rebalance_at insertions
the tree is rebuilt if its depth is more than 10 levels off the balanced depth. On
failure (no memory) the tree is unchanged.

<a id="tld_kdtree_rebalance"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_rebalance`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_rebalance(tld_kdtree *t);
```

Rebuild the tree balanced from the points it holds (allocates nothing).

<a id="tld_kdtree_nn_search"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_nn_search`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_nn_search(tld_kdtree *t, double *x, uint32_t *id);
```

The id of the stored point nearest to x (a vector of the tree's length) into *id.
FAIL (with an error) when the tree is empty.

<a id="tld_kdtree_bf_search"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_bf_search`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_bf_search(tld_kdtree *t, double *x, uint32_t *id);
```

Brute force: the id of the stored point nearest to x, comparing every point; FAIL
(with an error) when the tree is empty. For checking tld_kdtree_nn_search.

<a id="tld_kdtree_dist_euclidean"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_dist_euclidean`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_dist_euclidean(double *a, double *b, int vec_len, double *dist);
```

Squared Euclidean distance between a and b (vec_len doubles) into *dist. The default
fptr_cmp.

<a id="tld_kdtree_plane_euclidean"></a>

### `tld_kdtree_plane_euclidean`

```c
TLD_API  int tld_kdtree_plane_euclidean(double *a, double *b, int cd, double min_dist);
```

OK when the squared distance between a and b along dimension cd is below min_dist
(the far side of the splitting plane may hold a nearer point), FAIL otherwise. The
default fptr_plane.

<a id="mod-tpool"></a>

## tpool

`src/tpool/tld-tpool.h`: A pthread pool. Jobs func(pool, data, start, end, thread_id) are queued with tld_thread_pool_add and run in FIFO order by a fixed set of worker threads; optional time limit and a global stop flag.

<a id="tld_global_stop_run"></a><a id="tld_global_cond_mutex"></a><a id="tld_global_cond"></a>

### `tld_global_stop_run`, `tld_global_cond_mutex`, `tld_global_cond`

```c
TLD_API atomic_int tld_global_stop_run;
TLD_API pthread_mutex_t tld_global_cond_mutex;
TLD_API  pthread_cond_t tld_global_cond;
```

Global stop flag. The library installs no signal handlers: a program that wants to
stop running pools (e.g. on SIGINT) sets tld_global_stop_run = 1 itself; workers
check it between jobs and stop, dropping queued jobs. The mutex and condition are not
used by tld; they are there for programs that want to sleep until the flag is set.

<a id="tld_thread_pool"></a>

### `tld_thread_pool`

```c
typedef struct tld_thread_pool {
        struct tld__work_queue* work;
        int n_threads;
        int n_active_threads;
        int n_jobs_processed;
        /* Pausing */
        pthread_mutex_t lock;

        pthread_cond_t work_cond;
        pthread_cond_t working_cond;
        pthread_attr_t attr;

        pthread_t* threads;
        int64_t* thread_id_map;
        int thread_id_idx;
        int n_working;
        int stop;
        double maxtime;
        time_t internal_time;
        time_t stop_watch;
        int n_dropped;          /* jobs refused or abandoned after a stop */

} tld_thread_pool;
```

A thread pool; create with tld_thread_pool_alloc, free with tld_thread_pool_free.
The fields are internal (n_threads may be read).

<a id="tld_thread_pool_alloc"></a>

### `tld_thread_pool_alloc`

```c
TLD_API int  tld_thread_pool_alloc(tld_thread_pool **pool, double max_time, int n_threads);
```

Start a pool of n_threads workers (at least 2) in *pool. max_time is a limit in
minutes since creation, checked after each job: once passed, the pool stops and
queued jobs are dropped. 0 means no limit.

<a id="tld_thread_pool_add"></a>

### `tld_thread_pool_add`

```c
TLD_API int tld_thread_pool_add(tld_thread_pool *p, void (*func_ptr)(tld_thread_pool*,void *,int64_t, int64_t,int), void *data, int64_t start, int64_t end);
```

Queue a job: a worker calls func_ptr(p, data, start, end, thread_id), thread_id in
[0, n_threads). start and end are passed through (e.g. a slice of an index range).
Thread-safe; may be called from inside a job. Once the pool has stopped (time limit
or tld_global_stop_run) the job is refused: FAIL without a message, and data is still
the caller's to free.

<a id="tld_thread_pool_wait"></a>

### `tld_thread_pool_wait`

```c
TLD_API int tld_thread_pool_wait(tld_thread_pool *p);
```

Block until the queue is empty and no job is running (after a stop: until every
worker has exited). OK when every job added to the pool has run; FAIL, without a
message, when a stop refused or abandoned jobs (they did not run, so whatever they
would have done or freed did not happen). A running pool can take more jobs
afterwards. NULL is ignored (OK).

<a id="tld_thread_pool_free"></a>

### `tld_thread_pool_free`

```c
TLD_API void tld_thread_pool_free(tld_thread_pool *p);
```

Run every job still queued, then stop and join the workers and free the pool. NULL
is ignored.
